data.title: Probe D — the hypothesis about documents as linked context
body: # Probe D — the hypothesis about documents as linked context

- **Occasion:** an objection to the recommendation "do not build `kadence doc`". My analysis treated documents as separate files ("git already versions them"). The objection was about the **link**, not about storage — and git does not give that: it versions the file, but does not know that this file explains this task
- **Status:** **hypothesis confirmed by measurement**
## Hypothesis
> **If we** allow documents to be linked to tasks and decisions so that they come back together with the work in one call,
> **for** a developer and an agent taking on an unfamiliar task,
> **then** they will get the context they need without guessing which file out of dozens is the relevant one.
**What would make it false:** if an ordinary search already finds the needed document cheaply, the link adds nothing and is not worth building.
## Experiment
Cheap, local, without users — on the template of [Probe C](DOC-57).
Five real questions that face someone taking on work in this repository, and the document that answers each. For each, two paths were measured:

- **Today:** the agent runs `grep` for the natural term across `docs/`, `SPEC.md`, `README.md`, and has to **open the candidates** to work out which of them is relevant. The price is the sum of their bytes.
- **With the link:** one document, opened directly.
## Result
| Question | Term | Candidates | Bytes in the candidates | With the link | Difference |
| What must not be broken in the `--json` contract? | `json` | 27 | 327,870 | 7,241 | **45×** |
| Can a directory be added to the user's repository? | `git` | 35 | 407,796 | 6,520 | **62×** |
| Why is `board --json` a problem at scale? | `board` | 18 | 250,943 | 6,656 | **38×** |
| Which invariants govern folding? | `state` | 14 | 180,879 | 8,966 | **20×** |
| Why is conflict-freedom not the headline? | `conflict` | 10 | 154,049 | 9,318 | **17×** |
## What the measurement actually showed

**The search finds the answer in all five cases.** The problem is not that the document cannot be found — it is that it lies among 10–35 candidates, and to work out which of them is needed, they have to be opened.
That is, the link saves not the **search** but the **sifting**. And it is the sifting that costs context window.

**A stronger argument that does not depend on these numbers:** `grep` requires knowing the term. The whole bet of the product is that the agent does not know what it does not know. A link works without a search word — it arrives together with the task.
## Limitations that make the result weaker than it looks
1. **This is a document-heavy repository** — 37 documents to 4 tasks. In a typical project the ratio is different, and the difference will be smaller.

2. **The model "the agent opens every candidate" is an upper bound.** A sensible agent sifts by file name, and the names here are descriptive (`probe-c-agent-cost.md`). How much it would actually sift out could not be modelled honestly, so the true figure is **below 34×**, and by how much is unknown.
3. **I picked the questions knowing the answers.** This is the most serious bias in the experiment.
Even with a correction for all three — the gap between 154 KB of candidates and 9 KB of answer in the worst of the five cases is not explained by error.
## Decision
**The hypothesis is confirmed. We build — but not the way the request proposed, and not the way I argued against.**

Not `kadence doc` — that is, not a command that creates and stores documents. My earlier argument against that stands: git already versions files, and the event model gives a document nothing it does not already have.

But a **link**: a task and a decision can point at a document, and that document comes back together with them in `--json`. The document is written in ordinary Markdown, as it always was. kadence takes on the one thing git does not do — **it knows that this file concerns this work**.
This is the cheapest part of the plan and the largest difference in this measurement.
## What the probe did not answer

Whether anyone will put these links in. The measurement shows that the link is **valuable if it is there** — and says nothing about whether people will create it. This is the same hole as with `kadence decision`, and the same gate: [Probe B](DOC-49).
The difference is that the price of being wrong here is smaller: a link is a field in an event, not a separate subsystem.
